rationale: While EU DisinfoLab is a legitimate and well-regarded disinformation research platform, this particular publication focuses exclusively on Spain's domestic and EU-adjacent information environment—not on Russian imperialism, colonialism, or the Eastern European/Central Asian/Siberian regions that define DECOLONIAL.IST's scope. Topical fit is only 1 (general disinformation work, no decolonial or Russia/USSR angle). Geographic fit is 0 (Spain is explicitly out of scope). The outlet itself might be relevant for a Russia-focused FIMI factsheet, but this particular page is not. No CFP, deadline, or submission mechanism is indicated.

title: Other Grant Opportunities
summary: NEH grants listing page offering multiple US-focused humanities funding programs, none of which align with Russian colonialism, Eastern European/Central Asian regions, or decolonial knowledge infrastructure.
rationale: While NEH is a prestigious funder (reach 4), the visible opportunities are explicitly US-domestic: State Humanities Councils, Celebrate America, Curriculum Development in Western Civilization, Japan fellowship, American landmarks. None targets Russian/Soviet imperialism, post-Soviet regions, or decolonization. Geographic fit is 0 (US-centric). Topical fit is 1 (humanities broadly, no colonial/imperial angle visible). Eligibility flagged: NEH typically requires US-based organizations or individuals; we lack US legal entity status. The page itself is a search results listing, not a specific call—no actionable deadline extracted.

title: postcolonial literature
summary: WikiCFP aggregator page listing postcolonial literature conferences, mostly expired or with no geographic/thematic specificity to Russian colonialism or our regions.
rationale: This is a search-results page, not a live CFP. The listed conferences are either expired (2014–2020), lack regional/geographic focus (Nadine Gordimer, Arab Literature, generic postcolonial literature), or have no clear connection to Russian/Soviet imperialism or Eastern Europe/Central Asia/Caucasus. Topical score reflects generic 'postcolonial' framing without the Russian/Soviet or regional specificity we need. Geographic score is 0: no indication any listed event focuses on our regions. Feasibility and reach are moot given the absence of a current, live opportunity with clear submission criteria.

title: Postcolonial Ecofeminist Literature 2023
summary: A handbook chapter CFP on postcolonial ecofeminist literature focusing on Africa, the Middle East, Asia-Oceania, and the Americas—geographically and thematically misaligned with DECOLONIAL.IST's Russian/Soviet colonial focus and knowledge-infrastructure mission.
rationale: While the call invokes 'postcolonial' studies, it is entirely literary and ecological in focus, with no engagement with Russian/Soviet imperialism, Eastern Europe, the Caucasus, Central Asia, or the indigenous peoples within the Russian Federation. The geographic scope is explicitly non-European (or peripheral to Europe) and excludes the region central to DECOLONIAL.IST. The deadline has also passed (June 2023). Topical and geographic alignment are both minimal; this does not meet the threshold for relevance.

title: Central Europe and Colonialism 2016
summary: A 2016 conference on Central Europe's role in colonialism (both as colonizers in Western empires and colonized by Russia/USSR), with strong geographic fit but the event has already passed and the deadline was nearly a decade ago.
rationale: The conference is topically tangential: it addresses colonialism and Central Europe's ambiguous position vis-à-vis Russia, but focuses primarily on Central European participation in Western European colonial projects rather than Russian/Soviet colonialism as primary subject. Geographic scope includes Central Europe and Russia/USSR but the framing is backward-looking to 2016. Most critically: the submission deadline (30 Sep 2015) and event dates (21–23 Sep 2016) are both in the past—this opportunity is no longer actionable. Eligibility and feasibility scores are 0 because the event has concluded.

title: Call for Course Proposals: Online Lab on the Memory of the Syrian War
summary: Memory Studies Association online lab on Syrian war memory; geographically and topically misaligned with DECOLONIAL.IST's Russian colonialism focus.
rationale: While the call emphasizes memory studies and collaborative research on primary sources—methodologically resonant with our work—it is explicitly focused on the Syrian war, which falls outside our geographic scope (Eastern Europe, Caucasus, Central Asia, Siberia, Russian diaspora). Topical score reflects that memory studies is relevant but the Syrian context is unrelated to Russian/Soviet colonialism. Eligibility is unclear (scholars at risk may have different requirements than standard academic affiliation). Reach is modest (niche memory studies audience, no funding mentioned). Below relevance threshold.

title: UNDEF Civil Society Partners Hosted a Workshop at Nairobi Civil Society Conference
source: UN Democracy Fund — news & application rounds
summary: UN Democracy Fund workshop and funding stream focused on African civil society, women's leadership, and youth engagement — geographically and thematically outside DECOLONIAL.IST scope.
rationale: While UNDEF is a legitimate and well-resourced funding mechanism for civil society, this particular workshop and its framing are anchored in African democracy, women's empowerment in East Africa, and the Pact for the Future agenda. Geographic scope is explicitly Africa (Kenya, Tanzania, Ethiopia); our regions (Eastern Europe, Caucasus, Central Asia, Siberia) are not mentioned or plausible within this initiative. Topical fit is general governance/democracy/human rights without decolonial or Russian imperial content. Eligibility for future UNDEF calls may exist for informal groups, but this news item does not constitute an active call; no deadline is stated.

title: Empowering Media: Tajikistan's Civil Society's Bold Move to Safeguard Journalistic Freedom
source: UN Democracy Fund — news & application rounds
summary: A UN Democracy Fund news item about a completed media-freedom project in Tajikistan (2021–2023); not a live funding call or CFP.
rationale: This is a retrospective news article about a concluded project, not an open funding opportunity. No deadline, application process, or eligibility criteria are stated. Geographic fit is moderate (Central Asia, Tajikistan in scope). Topical fit is weak: the article focuses on journalistic freedom and legal literacy for media professionals, not on Russian colonialism or decolonization. While Tajikistan is within our regional scope, the framing is media-rights advocacy, not imperial history or OSINT/disinformation analysis. The UNDEF itself runs regular funding rounds, but this page does not constitute an open call.

title: Russian Studies – Master’s degree program
summary: A two-year accredited Master's program in Russian studies at Charles University (Prague) focusing on post-1991 Russia, foreign policy, and media — geographically well-placed but structured as a degree program, not a funding opportunity for external projects.
rationale: While the geographic scope (Eastern Europe, Russia) and institutional prestige are strong, this is a degree program, not a funding call or grant opportunity. DECOLONIAL.IST is neither a student cohort nor an academic department seeking to embed curriculum — it is an independent open knowledge base project. Topical fit is weak: the program's focus on post-1991 Russia, transition, and regime analysis does not explicitly address colonialism, decolonization, or the colonial history and structures that DECOLONIAL.IST documents. Eligibility and feasibility are both 0 because there is no mechanism for a volunteer project to apply; the program accepts individual student candidates. Not relevant as structured.

title: Russia Orders Arrest in Absentia of Zhanna Nemtsova
summary: News article about arrest warrant for Zhanna Nemtsova; covers Russian repression but is not a funding call, CFP, or collaboration opportunity.
rationale: This is a news article, not a funding opportunity, conference CFP, or media outlet invitation. While it documents Russian state repression in the region (geographic 5) and has some relevance to our work on Russian authoritarianism, it is neither a call we can apply to nor a venue that solicits contributions. Topical score reflects that the article itself is news reporting rather than a scholarly or institutional call aligned with our decolonial framework. No actionable deadline or eligibility pathway exists.

title: Statement by participants of the Platform of Russian Democratic Forces at PACE on the anniversary of the murder of Boris Nemtsov:“We have no doubt that Vladimir Putin stands behind the murder of Boris Nemtsov.”
summary: A political statement by Russian democratic opposition figures commemorating Boris Nemtsov's assassination and calling for accountability — important activism but not a funding opportunity or publication venue.
rationale: This is a commemorative statement/press release from the Boris Nemtsov Foundation, not a funding call, conference, media outlet, or grant application opportunity. While it is geographically and politically aligned with anti-colonial/anti-authoritarian work and published by a respected Russian democratic organization, there is no stated call for submissions, funding, partnerships, or collaborative projects. The topical fit is weak (opposition politics and human rights accountability, not colonial studies or knowledge infrastructure). No eligibility, feasibility, or reach dimensions apply to a news statement. Not actionable for DECOLONIAL.IST.

title: Postcolonial Ecofeminist Literature 2023
summary: A handbook chapter call on postcolonial ecofeminist literature covering Africa, Middle East, Asia, Oceania, Americas, and Europe — geographically excludes our core regions and topically misaligned with historical/political analysis of colonial TTPs.
rationale: While postcolonial studies is relevant to decolonial work, this opportunity is explicitly literary and ecofeminist in focus, with no mention of empire, colonization tactics, disinformation, or the specific geographies central to DECOLONIAL.IST (Eastern Europe, Caucasus, Central Asia, Siberia, Russia/USSR). The geographic scope lists Africa, Middle East, Asia, Oceania, Americas, and Europe — but no specific mention of Eastern Europe, the post-Soviet space, or our target regions; Russia/USSR is not indexed. The deadline (June 2023) has also already passed. Eligibility for chapter contributors is open, but topical fit is too distant to pursue.

title: Russia's Soft-Power in Europe 2017
summary: Panel on Russian soft-power and information strategies in Europe at the 7th International Congress of Belarusian Studies (2017).
rationale: Topical score is low (2): the CFP focuses on Russian influence operations and propaganda, which is tangential to DECOLONIAL.IST's core mission of documenting colonization tactics grounded in historical experience of colonized peoples. Geographic fit is moderate (4): Belarus and Eastern Europe are in scope, but the framing is about foreign interference rather than colonialism or decolonization per se. Eligibility and feasibility are both 0: the deadline (May 10, 2017) has long passed—this is a retrospective listing from 2017. Reach is low (2): a single panel at a regional studies congress. This opportunity is not actionable.

title: Infrastructure Grants
source: House of Europe (EU–Ukraine, grants in UK/EN)
summary: House of Europe Infrastructure Grants fund physical cultural spaces (cinemas, museums, rehearsal halls) in Ukraine and small towns, not knowledge bases or digital projects.
rationale: While the grant is geographically perfect (Ukraine-focused), the topical fit is poor: these are capital infrastructure grants for renovating physical buildings and purchasing equipment (projectors, paint, seating), explicitly designed for 'cultural spaces' like museums and cinemas. DECOLONIAL.IST is a digital knowledge base with no physical infrastructure needs. Eligibility is blocked: the grant requires a registered NGO ('active cultural NGOs'), and the project lacks legal-entity status. The €10–99k range is solid, but the entire structure is misaligned with a digital research/educational project.

title: Відбір нових громад для участі в канадському проєкті “Відновлення для всіх” (RFA)
summary: Canadian-funded community recovery program for Ukrainian territorial communities affected by war, focused on development strategies and local service delivery.
rationale: While geographically targeted at Ukraine (perfect fit for scope), this is fundamentally a post-conflict reconstruction and municipal development program with no decolonial, imperial studies, or knowledge-infrastructure dimensions. Topical fit is minimal—it addresses war recovery and social services, not colonialism or decolonization. Eligibility is zero: applications must come from local government bodies (municipal councils or military administrations) representing communities under 20,000 people in specific regions. DECOLONIAL.IST is a volunteer knowledge-base project, not a territorial community, and cannot meet the legal/governance requirements. Not suitable.

title: «Траєкторія 3»: до 1 000 000 грн на масштабування ветеранського та дружнього до ветеранів бізнесу
summary: Ukrainian veteran and veteran-friendly business scaling grant (up to 1M UAH) — geographically relevant but structurally incompatible with DECOLONIAL.IST's mission and legal status.
rationale: This is a business-development grant explicitly for for-profit enterprises (manufacturers, B2B services) founded by or employing military veterans. DECOLONIAL.IST is a volunteer knowledge-base project, not a business, and has no commercial revenue or scaling agenda. Topical fit is negligible (business scaling ≠ decolonial knowledge work). Eligibility is zero: the call requires operative businesses with business plans; we are an unfunded collective without legal entity status. Feasibility is zero: this is not a fit regardless of capacity. Geographic scope is Ukrainian, which favors Ukrainian applicants and entities. Do not pursue.

title: В Одесі стартував проєкт зі створення кроссекторальної цифрової платформи дослідження козацьких хрестів Куяльницького кладовища
summary: A completed Ukrainian cultural-heritage project documenting Cossack crosses at a cemetery in Odesa, already funded and launched by a partner NGO—not an open opportunity.
rationale: This is a news announcement of a project that has already started (dated 04.08.2026), not a call for applications or funding. The project is being led by ГО Піксельовані Реальності with Greek partner Talent S.A., already funded by Український культурний фонд. While the geographic scope (Ukraine/Odesa) and decolonial framing ('deconstructing colonial myths') align with DECOLONIAL.IST's mission, this is not an opportunity to apply or participate. Topical score reflects that Ukrainian heritage documentation, though regional and decolonial in spirit, does not directly concern Russian/Soviet colonization tactics and procedures as DECOLONIAL.IST documents them.

title: Engaging Armenian Youth in Local Governance
source: UN Democracy Fund — news & application rounds
summary: UNDEF news item about a completed/ongoing Armenian youth governance project — geographically relevant but topically misaligned and not an open call.
rationale: This is a news article announcing an already-funded project by the A.D. Sakharov Armenian Human Rights Protection Centre, not an open funding opportunity or call for applications. Topical fit is weak: while Armenia is in our geographic scope, the project focuses on youth participation in local governance and leadership development, not colonialism, decolonization, or Russian imperialism. No application deadline or mechanism is stated. Not relevant as a funding opportunity for DECOLONIAL.IST.

title: Connections through Culture: grants for cultural projects with Great Britain Deadline: 12 August 2026 at 23:59 Kyiv time
source: House of Europe (EU–Ukraine, grants in UK/EN)
summary: EUR 12k cultural exchange grant between Ukraine and Great Britain for artists and cultural organizations in architecture, design, film, music, theatre, and digital arts.
rationale: While geographically well-placed (Ukraine-UK partnership, Ukrainian applicants welcome), this opportunity is fundamentally misaligned: it targets visual/performing artists and creative practitioners in architecture, design, fashion, film, music, theatre, and dance — not knowledge infrastructure, research, or documentation projects. DECOLONIAL.IST is neither a cultural/creative organization nor an artist collective; it is a scholarly knowledge base. Eligibility is also blocked: the grant requires Ukrainian registration (individual entrepreneur, LLC, charity foundation, public/state organization), and DECOLONIAL.IST is currently an unregistered volunteer collective without legal entity status. The topical fit is minimal (culture broadly, but not the decolonial/empire scholarship or knowledge documentation that defines our work). Not recommended.

title: What is it like to be among the first? Piotr Marecki on introducing Ukrainian literature to Poland
source: House of Europe (EU–Ukraine, grants in UK/EN)
summary: A House of Europe success story profiling a Polish publisher's work translating Ukrainian literature into Polish — geographically relevant but not topically aligned with DECOLONIAL.IST's focus on colonial tactics and historical/contemporary imperialism.
rationale: This is a profile piece, not a funding call or CFP — it documents past grant recipients rather than offering an opportunity to apply. Topically, it centers literary translation and Polish-Ukrainian cultural exchange, not colonialism, decolonization, or knowledge infrastructure on imperialism. Geographic fit is strong (Eastern Europe, Poland–Ukraine), but the project's mission and audience (literary scholars, translators, publishers) do not overlap with DECOLONIAL.IST's work on imperial domination tactics or disinformation/OSINT analysis. No eligibility pathway is evident.

title: EU- Eastern Europe 2014
summary: Economics-focused panel on Central East European trade and development integration; no colonial or decolonial angle.
rationale: Topical score is 1: while the conference concerns Eastern Europe, it is narrowly framed around neoliberal economic transition and EU integration, with no engagement with imperialism, colonization, or decolonization. Geographic score is 3: Eastern Europe is in scope but the framing is explicitly economic/developmental, not political or historical. Eligibility and feasibility are both 0: the deadline (Feb 25, 2014) passed over a decade ago. This opportunity is archival only and not actionable.

title: Women Leadership and Climate-Smart Agriculture: A New Chapter for Armenian Women Farmers
source: UN Democracy Fund — news & application rounds
summary: UNDEF-funded project supporting Armenian women farmers in climate-smart agriculture and local leadership; geographically in scope but thematically unrelated to documenting colonialism or decolonization.
rationale: While Armenia is in our geographic scope (Caucasus), this opportunity is focused on climate adaptation and women's agricultural leadership—not imperialism, colonization, decolonization, or knowledge infrastructure around colonial history. Topical fit is minimal. Eligibility is unclear: the snippet describes a completed/ongoing project led by a registered Armenian NGO (AWHHE), not an open funding call; no application deadline or process is stated. Even if a call exists, DECOLONIAL.IST would need Armenian legal-entity status or a local partner to be competitive. Not a fit for our mission or capacity.

title: Russia: Statement by the Spokesperson marking eleven years since the murder of Boris Nemtsov in Moscow
summary: EU statement commemorating Boris Nemtsov's assassination; not a funding call, CFP, or partnership opportunity.
rationale: This is a press statement marking a political assassination and EU human-rights stance, not a solicitation for proposals, grants, or collaboration. While it concerns Russia and human rights (geographic 5), it is not a funding call, conference CFP, or media outlet seeking contributions. The topical score (1) reflects that this is political commemoration rather than decolonial scholarship or knowledge infrastructure. No deadline, eligibility pathway, or actionable opportunity exists for DECOLONIAL.IST to engage with this text.

title: central and eastern europe
summary: A WikiCFP aggregate page listing historical and expired Central and Eastern Europe conference calls, with no active opportunities and no thematic specificity.
rationale: This is a database index page, not an actual CFP. All listed conferences are either expired (2016–2024) or lack detailed information. The geographic scope (CEE) is relevant, but without active deadlines, submission guidelines, or thematic descriptions, this cannot be scored as a real opportunity. The BPM forum (business process management) and white-collar education entries have no colonial/decolonial angle. This requires human navigation to actual live CFPs, which should be evaluated individually.

title: The Eastern Siberia Oil & Gas Conference 2014

rationale: This is an extractive-industry trade conference focused on energy development in Eastern Siberia and the Russian Far East — geographically within our scope but thematically orthogonal to decolonization, empire studies, or knowledge infrastructure. The conference is also a decade old (deadline passed long ago). No colonialism angle, no indigenous-peoples or minority-rights dimension, no academic or advocacy fit. Not relevant.

DECOLONIAL.IST is a knowledge base; it does not provide or coordinate vehicle services. Ineligible and infeasible.

DECOLONIAL.IST is a volunteer collective project, not an employer, and cannot apply for staff positions. The opportunity is ineligible by nature.
